headline: Discussed brochure translation languages, fair housing plan coordination, and a 13 Albion Street complaint; agreed to use multilingual QR codes at events.
summary: Members discussed which languages to translate brochures into and planned to check census data and city website analytics. They also discussed the city's comprehensive plan and the 13 Albion Street housing complaint, where complainants have not responded for several months. Members agreed to use QR codes linking to the city website in multiple languages until brochure translations are ready.
decisions: Agreed to use QR codes linking to the city website in multiple languages until brochure translations are ready. No vote was recorded.

Meeting started at 5:55 PM
Brochure Translation Language Selection: Paul led a discussion with Taylor, Cindy, Elaine, and Madelein 
McCormick (SEN) on which languages the Human Rights and Fair Housing Commission's brochures 
should be translated into, considering community demographics and input from Maria, with a plan to 
consult census data and city website analytics before finalizing the choices.
Fair Housing Plan Coordination: Paul updated the group on the city's comprehensive plan being 
developed by OSPCD under Alex Pratt, discussed the need for ongoing commission involvement, and 
proposed inviting department representatives to future meetings for direct updates and input.
Follow-Up on Albion Street Housing Complaint: Paul and Taylor reviewed the status of a previous 
housing complaint from 13 Albion Street, noting that after extensive communication and guidance, the 
complainants have not responded for several months, and Maria may follow up for any further needs.

Event Planning and Outreach Materials: Malden, Taylor, and Madelein McCormick (SEN) discussed 
upcoming outreach events, including Public Safety Day and National Night Out, and agreed to use QR 
codes linking to the city website in multiple languages until brochure translations are ready.
Follow-up tasks
Brochure Translation Languages: Obtain and review Malden's census or city website data to determine 
the most prevalent languages spoken in the community for brochure translation selection. (Paul)
Brochure Translation Languages: Follow up with Maria to confirm which languages should be prioritized
for brochure translation based on population data and commission discussion. (Malden).
Fair Housing Plan Coordination: Contact Maria to arrange for a representative from OSPCD (Alex Pratt's 
department) to attend next month's meeting and provide an update on the comprehensive plan and fair
housing resources. (Paul).
Complaint Follow-Up: Follow up with Maria regarding the status and any updates on the 13 Albion 
Street complaint, including whether further contact with the household is needed. (Paul).
Event Materials Accessibility: Create and print a multilingual QR code sign for the October Public Safety 
Day event table, directing attendees to the city website for information in their preferred language until 
brochure translations are available. (Madelein, Taylor)
Meeting Adjourned at 6:27
